hawkish.title: Oct 28 FOMC hold on a 10-2 vote: Cook and Hammack dissent for +25bp
hawkish.summary: Two voters wanted an immediate hike; statement kept elevated-inflation bias and strong-growth wording.

data.actual: Hold 3.75-4.00%, 10-2 (Cook, Hammack for +25bp)

hawkish.reason: Two dissents in favour of an immediate hike show the hawkish wing is not waiting for December; together with unchanged 'inflation remains elevated' language this kept the bar for a December move low rather than signalling a pause.
hawkish.market_validation: Kalshi Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.79 at the 14:00 ET hourly close -> 0.80-0.81 in the 15:00-16:00 ET hours on 28 Oct (76.9k contracts in the decision hour).

hawkish.title: October payrolls +165,000, unemployment 4.1%: no cooling ahead of 9 December
hawkish.summary: Strong job beat with +84k prior revisions removes labour-slack cover for another December pause.

data.actual: +165k payrolls; unemployment 4.1%; AHE +0.4% m/m, +3.1% y/y
data.delta_label: +100k vs consensus; +84k of upward revisions; unemployment -0.1pp

hawkish.reason: The most recent payroll report available at this snapshot beat consensus by 100,000 with 84,000 of upward revisions and a falling unemployment rate, weakening the slack argument for holding. It is not the final report before the decision: November payrolls are scheduled for 4 December. The broad gains and +0.4% monthly wages matter for inflation, but upcoming PCE and employment releases can change the outlook.
hawkish.market_validation: Kalshi Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.64/0.65 (mid 0.645) at the 5 Nov close (23:00 ET) -> 0.78/0.79 (mid 0.785) in the 09:00 ET candle on 6 Nov, +14.0pp across the 08:30 ET release on 68,547 contracts; Polymarket's 25bp leg went 0.655 (5 Nov 23:00 ET) -> 0.785 (6 Nov 09:00 ET), and Reuters reported bets rising 'to 78% following the data from 70% earlier'. The print reversed the 5 November sell-off rather than setting a new high: the leg had closed 4 November at 0.79/0.80.

hawkish.title: Hammack: policy 'will need to move to a restrictive stance' to get inflation back to 2%
hawkish.summary: October dissenter says policy must turn restrictive to return inflation to 2% on time.

data.actual: "monetary policy will need to move to a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to 2 percent in a timely manner"
data.previous: 28 Oct: dissented for +25bp while the Committee held
data.delta_label: explicit call for a restrictive stance

hawkish.reason: One of the two votes for an immediate hike is now saying policy has to become restrictive, not merely less accommodative - a stronger formulation than the Committee's own statement - which keeps the hawkish wing's bar for December low.
hawkish.market_validation: No hawkish repricing on the day and none credited here: the Kalshi Dec 25bp-Hike leg fell from 0.79/0.80 (09:00 ET) to 0.64/0.65 by 17:00 ET on 5 Nov, then recovered to 0.78/0.79 in the 6 Nov payroll hour, so the session's 15pp swing is not attributable to her remarks.

hawkish.title: Waller: leaning to a December hike, 50bp 'should be considered' if core CPI is 0.3%
hawkish.summary: Governor leans toward a 25bp December hike and warns 50bp warrants consideration if core stays sticky.

data.actual: "I am leaning toward supporting an increase in our policy rate of 25 basis points at the FOMC's December meeting ... I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered"
data.previous: no size guidance from a Governor earlier in the cycle

hawkish.reason: Waller's personal inclination toward a December increase and conditional discussion of 50bp strengthen the hawkish communication signal. His views do not bind the Committee, establish a 25bp floor, or remove a hold option. Subsequent inflation, employment and financial-condition evidence can change the decision.
hawkish.market_validation: Kalshi Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.80/0.81 (mid 0.805) at 04:00 ET -> 0.88/0.89 (mid 0.885) at 05:00 ET on 10 Nov, +8.0pp on 28,077 contracts; the >25bp leg (H26) went 0.01/0.02 -> 0.02/0.03 in the same hour on 748,703 contracts and 0.04/0.06 by 06:00 ET.

hawkish.title: October CPI +0.4% m/m, core +0.3% a third straight month
hawkish.summary: Third straight 0.3% monthly core gain keeps tightening pressure on the Committee.

data.actual: +0.4% m/m, core +0.3% m/m (12-month change not published)
data.delta_label: +0.1pp on headline and core; third straight 0.3% core

hawkish.reason: Three consecutive 0.3% monthly core readings support the inflation concern behind Waller's personal, conditional discussion of a larger move. They do not guarantee a December increase or its size. October PCE and November employment data remain due before the decision, and the Committee retains discretion.
hawkish.market_validation: At the 08:30 ET print the Kalshi >25bp leg (H26) went from 0.05/0.06 (mid 0.055) at 08:00 ET to 0.10/0.11 (mid 0.105) at 09:00 ET and 0.12/0.14 at 10:00 ET on 345,470 contracts, +5.0pp, while the 25bp leg slipped from 0.86/0.87 to 0.85/0.86 as the size mix shifted.

hawkish.title: Jefferson: October data 'consistent with well above-target inflation', inflation is the signal
hawkish.summary: Vice Chair treats inflation trajectory as the primary policy signal while staying data-dependent.

data.actual: "The trajectory of inflation as providing the more important signal ... data received so far for October remains consistent with well above-target inflation"
data.previous: 28 Oct: voted with the majority to hold

hawkish.reason: Jefferson gives inflation the more important signal in his assessment, alongside activity, labour conditions, the evolving outlook and the balance of risks. This is a modest hawkish interpretation of his emphasis, not an inflation-only mandate or a December commitment; his data-dependent framing remains a counterweight.
hawkish.market_validation: unverified (the remarks landed after the 13 Nov cash close; the 13 Nov 09:00 ET candle move belongs to the 08:30 PPI print, not to this speech)

hawkish.title: Bowman: persistent inflation and firmer labour, with policy still data-dependent
hawkish.summary: Flags persistent inflation and firming labour, tempered by tighter financial conditions and rate sensitivity.

data.actual: Inflation persistence and firmer labour; financial-condition risks; no December commitment
data.delta_label: Moderate inflation concern, conditional policy path

hawkish.reason: Inflation concern supports a modest hawkish interpretation, rather than a promised hike. The acknowledged financing and activity risks temper this interpretation. The proposed two-point weight is an analytical judgment, not a fact or an inferred market reaction.
hawkish.market_validation: unverified (no speech-specific repricing established; no market move attributed)

hawkish.title: Williams: more hikes likely as AI investment feeds demand, but 'not the time for dramatic action'
hawkish.summary: Expects further tightening as AI demand lifts growth, while pushing back against 50bp steps.

data.actual: "We still have our work to do to make sure that we bring inflation back down to 2%" / "I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action"
data.previous: 13 Nov (Reuters): 'We'll need to take actions over time' to return inflation to 2%
data.delta_label: hawkish direction, explicit cap on size

hawkish.reason: A permanent voter and the committee's centre of gravity expects further tightening, which underwrites the December hike already priced, while his explicit rejection of 'dramatic action' caps the 50bp tail. The two halves matter separately: direction stays hawkish, size guidance does not.
hawkish.market_validation: Kalshi Dec >25bp leg 0.05/0.06 (mid 0.055) at 12:00 ET -> 0.04/0.05 (mid 0.045) at 13:00 ET and held there through 17:00 ET on 19,102-24,039 contracts per hour, while the 25bp leg sat at 0.90/0.91 all session: the remarks cut the size premium, not the direction.

hawkish.title: Hammack: inflation worsening and broadening, prefers steady consecutive hikes
hawkish.summary: October dissenter favors steady consecutive 25bp hikes as inflation broadens.

data.actual: "I like moving in smaller increments" - steady hikes, larger steps only 'if we get behind the curve'
data.previous: 28 Oct: dissented for +25bp while the Committee held
data.delta_label: a sequence of hikes, not a one-off

hawkish.reason: A 2026 voter and an October dissenter is describing a path of consecutive increases rather than a single move, which raises the bar for a December hold and makes 25bp the base case rather than the ceiling. Her size preference is the dovish half and is why this is not scored higher.
hawkish.market_validation: unverified (the interview aired in the Monday morning session and no speech-specific repricing can be isolated; the 25bp leg sat at 0.88/0.89 through the 11:00-14:00 ET hours on 16 Nov)

hawkish.title: October retail sales: +0.2% headline, control group +0.6% against 0.4% expected
hawkish.summary: Resilient control-group spending shows domestic demand absorbing current rates without slowing.

data.actual: +0.2% m/m total; control group +0.6%; ex-autos +0.6%
data.forecast: +0.2% total; control +0.4%; ex-autos +0.4% (Reuters poll / Action Economics)
data.delta_label: control +0.2pp vs consensus with upward revisions

hawkish.reason: Headline growth slowed only because autos fell; the control group that feeds GDP beat by 0.2pp and the prior two months were revised up. Household demand holding up at 3.1% CPI argues against treating policy as already restrictive, which supports a December hike but says nothing about 50bp.
hawkish.market_validation: Kalshi Dec >25bp leg 0.05/0.06 (mid 0.055) at 08:00 ET -> 0.06/0.07 (mid 0.065) in the 09:00 ET hour and 0.07/0.08 at 10:00 ET on 22,415 and 21,121 contracts, back to 0.05/0.06 by 11:00 ET; the 25bp leg slipped 0.90/0.91 -> 0.89/0.90, so the print bought size rather than direction.

hawkish.title: October FOMC minutes: 'almost all' saw further hikes as appropriate, a couple floated more than 25bp
hawkish.summary: Committee record shows October hold barely won and nearly all back more hikes if inflation stalls.

data.actual: "almost all participants judged ... further action to raise the target range ... would likely be appropriate"
data.previous: 28 Oct statement: hold, with two dissents for +25bp
data.delta_label: committee-level confirmation plus a live >25bp option

hawkish.reason: The minutes are the only committee-level record between the October hold and 9 December, and they confirm a December increase as the baseline rather than a market artefact. The same document keeps the size question open - 'a couple' want more than 25bp on the table - which is exactly the two-sided shape the ladder trades, so this is scored for direction only.
hawkish.market_validation: Kalshi Dec >25bp leg 0.06/0.07 (mid 0.065) at the 14:00 ET release -> 0.07/0.08 (mid 0.075) at the 16:00 ET candle on 19,331 and 3,721 contracts, while the 25bp leg eased 0.92/0.93 -> 0.90/0.91: the minutes bought the size tail, not new direction.

hawkish.title: Barr: 'I expect it will be appropriate to raise rates further'
hawkish.summary: Sitting Governor expects further rate increases if growth and inflation follow baseline.

data.actual: "I expect it will be appropriate to raise rates further"
data.previous: 28 Oct: voted with the majority to hold
data.delta_label: explicit further-tightening expectation, no size signal

hawkish.reason: A sitting Governor stating an expectation of further increases adds a voter to the direction case without touching size, so it is scored at the minimum weight: the ledger already carries stronger, earlier statements of the same view and this one changes no probability.
hawkish.market_validation: unverified (no size signal; the 25bp leg held 0.90/0.91 through the afternoon and the 1c rise in the >25bp leg at 16:00 ET is credited to the minutes released two hours earlier, not to this speech)

hawkish.title: Cook: a steady rate widens the output gap; inflation above target for more than five and a half years
hawkish.summary: October dissenter warns holding steady widens the positive output gap after five-plus years above target.

data.actual: "holding our policy rate steady will lead to a positive and widening output gap and increasing inflationary pressure"
data.previous: 28 Oct: dissented for +25bp while the Committee held
data.delta_label: dissenting Governor restates the case; no size signal

hawkish.reason: A sitting Governor and October dissenter arguing that standing still is itself accommodative supports the December direction case. It adds no size information and binds no other voter, so it carries a minimal weight rather than a larger one.
hawkish.market_validation: unverified (delivered at a conference in Santiago with no December-specific repricing that can be isolated: the Kalshi Dec 25bp leg dipped 0.90/0.91 -> 0.88/0.89 in the 12:00 ET hour on 20 Nov and was back at 0.89/0.90 by 15:00 ET, on 49,177 then 41,686 contracts)

hawkish.title: Williams Nov 23: inflation ~3.5%, 'still work to do'
hawkish.summary: NY Fed chief warns strong 2.75% growth requires further action over time to restore 2% inflation.

data.actual: 2026 GDP ~2.75%, PCE ~3.5%; 'We must take actions over time'

hawkish.reason: Williams linked resilient demand and AI-driven investment to above-target ~3.5% inflation, reinforcing the baseline for further policy action.
hawkish.market_validation: unverified (Kalshi 25bp leg held ~0.91-0.92 through Nov 23-25; no separate speech move isolated)

hawkish.title: Q3 GDP revised up to 4.3%, private final sales 5.8%
hawkish.summary: Stronger revision leaves demand above potential, keeping a December hike the base case.

data.actual: Real GDP +4.3% SAAR (advance +3.4%); final sales to private domestic purchasers +5.8% (from +4.9%); GDP price index 2.7%
data.forecast: n/a (second estimate; revision, not a consensus release)

hawkish.reason: The 0.9pp revision came from investment and consumer spending, so the strength is final demand rather than inventories; with private final sales at 5.8% the economy is not cooling into December. The GDP price index was revised down to 2.7%, which makes the real growth signal stronger, not weaker.
hawkish.market_validation: No net repricing on Kalshi: the Dec 25bp leg held 0.92/0.93 across the 13:30Z release (2,105 contracts in the 13:35Z minute) and the >25bp leg stayed 0.03/0.04, so the print confirmed rather than changed the hike price.

hawkish.title: October core PCE 3.3% y/y, +0.3% m/m again
hawkish.summary: Sticky core inflation on the Fed's preferred gauge keeps tightening pressure into December.

data.actual: Core PCE +0.3% m/m, +3.3% y/y; headline +0.3% m/m, +3.8% y/y; real PCE -0.1%

hawkish.reason: Core PCE at 3.3% is more than a point above target and the monthly pace did not slow, so the disinflation case for pausing in December is not supported by the Fed's preferred measure. Real spending slipped less than 0.1%, so the inflation is not the residue of collapsing volumes.
hawkish.market_validation: Kalshi Dec 25bp leg 0.92/0.93 unchanged from the 13:25Z pre-release minute through 14:10Z; the >25bp leg held 0.03/0.04 throughout, so no incremental repricing is attributed to this print.

dovish.title: Warsh: no forward guidance, 'I don't believe in prejudging meetings'
dovish.summary: Chair refuses December pre-commitment and notes improving inflation compensation.

data.actual: "I don't believe in forward guidance absent exigent circumstances ... I also don't believe in prejudging meetings."
data.previous: Sep SEP: 2026 median 4.1% (full range 3.9-4.4), i.e. the dots implied one more hike

dovish.reason: Refusing to endorse the September dots and pointing to improving inflation compensation keeps a December hold possible. The market did not trade it as dovish on the day, so it is scored as a modest offset only.
dovish.market_validation: unverified (Kalshi Dec 25bp-Hike leg did not fall during the presser; it rose 0.79 -> 0.81)

dovish.title: Sep real spending flat, real disposable income -0.3%
dovish.summary: Inflation eroding real income (-0.3%) left real Q3 exit spending flat.

data.actual: Real PCE <+0.1% m/m; real DPI -0.3%; nominal spending +0.5%

dovish.reason: Inflation is cutting into real income and real consumption stalled at the end of Q3; a further squeeze argues for patience because demand may cool without another hike.
dovish.market_validation: Kalshi Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.80 -> 0.75 between the 09:00 and 10:00 ET hourly closes on 29 Oct and 0.74 by 18:00 ET; attribution to this facet is not verified.

dovish.title: Warsh uses his first post-meeting speech on AI productivity, not December
dovish.summary: Chair focused his main November address on AI productivity rather than endorsing a December hike.

data.previous: 28 Oct press conference: "I don't believe in prejudging meetings"

dovish.reason: The Chair had the week's largest platform and used it for a productivity agenda rather than to endorse the hike his colleagues are guiding toward. With a hike around 96% priced, silence at the top is a marginal offset at best, which is why it scores 1.
dovish.market_validation: Kalshi Dec 25bp leg unchanged at 0.88/0.89 through the 12:00 ET remarks; the >25bp leg's mid eased 0.085 -> 0.075 in that hour on 113,079 contracts and 0.065 by 14:00 ET, so the speech cost the size premium, not the direction.

hawkish.title: Hike to 2.50%; CPI seen at 'about 3.5%' by year-end, averaging 3% in 2027
hawkish.summary: Hike lifted inflation path to ~3.5% year-end and 3% in 2027, keeping tightening bias open.

data.actual: +25bp to 2.50%; CPI about 3.5% by end-2026, 3% average 2027 (MPR 2.9% / 3.1%)
data.forecast: +25bp; no published consensus and no independently re-verified pre-release venue print

hawkish.reason: The Bank now projects inflation at about 3.5% by year-end and around 3% through 2027, kept an explicit tightening bias, and attributed the revision to energy prices it expects to stay higher for longer, so December stays a live meeting. No surprise credit is assigned because the pre-decision consensus and venue prints are not verifiable at this snapshot.
hawkish.market_validation: Kalshi BoC Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.47/0.49 before the release, first traded 0.46 at 09:45 ET and fell to 0.33-0.35 within 12 minutes, rebounded to 0.39-0.40 by mid-afternoon and sat at 0.37 on 29 Oct (about -11c net from the pre-release mid), so the market read the release as less hawkish for December than the projection alone implies. Post-decision swaps ~60% for a December hike (Bloomberg data via The Globe and Mail, 28 Oct) - secondary, not independently verified.

hawkish.title: Growth outlook upgraded: Q2 3.3%, Q3 ~2%, 'somewhat stronger' than July
hawkish.summary: Upgraded medium-term growth path reduces excess supply buffer against energy shocks.
hawkish.reason: The Bank's Q3 indicators pointed to growth of about 2%, and its projected growth path was stronger than in July. This is a tracking estimate and outlook, not a released Q3 GDP outturn; the official Q3 release is scheduled for 30 November. The stronger projected path modestly weakens the slack argument for holding, conditional on subsequent data.

data.previous: 28 Oct press release: same tightening bias, no deliberation record

It scores 2 rather than more because it restates the decision's own logic and adds no new data.
hawkish.market_validation: unverified (published at the Bank's 13:30 ET slot on 10 Nov; no release-window repricing is isolated for this snapshot)

dovish.summary: Governor laid out the careful one-meeting-at-a-time approach given core near 2% and tariff headwinds.

dovish.market_validation: Kalshi BoC Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.48/0.49 (mid 0.485) at 08:00 ET -> 0.46/0.47 (mid 0.465) at 09:00 ET on 16 Nov, -2.0pp on 323 contracts; the book had already fallen from 0.54/0.55 on 13 Nov, so the print trimmed an existing hawkish position rather than reversing one.
